def word_wrap(text, width):
    """Greedy wrap. Words are separated only by the space character; tabs,
    new lines and hyphens are part of a word. Each line holds as many words
    as fit within width, joined by one space. A word longer than width is
    cut into pieces of width characters, each on its own line, and the last
    piece starts the next line. Raises ValueError when width < 1."""
    if width < 1:
        raise ValueError("width < 1")
    words = [w for w in text.split(" ") if w]
    lines = []
    cur = []
    for w in words:
        while len(w) > width:
            if cur:
                lines.append(" ".join(cur))
                cur = []
            lines.append(w[:width])
            w = w[width:]
        candidate = cur + [w]
        if len(" ".join(candidate)) <= width:
            cur = candidate
        else:
            lines.append(" ".join(cur))
            cur = [w]
    if cur:
        lines.append(" ".join(cur))
    return lines

Runs the visible tests on candidate.py, then times candidate.py against
original.py on the benchmark input (best of 5 runs)."""
import copy
import importlib.util
import os
import time

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
FUNC = 'word_wrap'
TESTS = [(('the quick brown fox', 10), ['the quick', 'brown fox']), (('a b c', 1), ['a', 'b', 'c'])]
BENCH_SRC = "import random\n_r = random.Random(7)\nARGS = (' '.join(''.join(_r.choice('abcdefgh') for _ in range(_r.randint(1, 8))) for _ in range(20000)), 400)"
TARGET = 2.0  # None means no speed target


def load(name):
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, os.path.join(HERE, name + ".py"))
    m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(m)
    return getattr(m, FUNC)


def best(fn, args, reps=5):
    t_best = float("inf")
    for _ in range(reps):
        a = copy.deepcopy(args)
        t = time.perf_counter()
        fn(*a)
        t_best = min(t_best, time.perf_counter() - t)
    return t_best


ref, cand = load("original"), load("candidate")
ok = True
for args, want in TESTS:
    try:
        got = cand(*copy.deepcopy(args))
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        got = "raised " + type(e).__name__
    if got != want:
        ok = False
        print("FAIL %s%r: want %r, got %r" % (FUNC, args, want, got))
if ok:
    print("tests: all %d passed" % len(TESTS))

env = {}
exec(BENCH_SRC, env)
speed = best(ref, env["ARGS"]) / best(cand, env["ARGS"])
print("speed: %.2fx faster than original" % speed)

if TARGET is not None and speed < TARGET:
    ok = False
    print("speed is below the %.1fx target" % TARGET)
print("ACCEPTED" if ok else "NOT ACCEPTED")

{"content":"import re


def word_wrap(text, width):
    """Greedy wrap. Words are separated only by the space character; tabs,
    new lines and hyphens are part of a word. Each line holds as many words
    as fit within width, joined by one space. A word longer than width is
    cut into pieces of width characters, each on its own line, and the last
    piece starts the next line. Raises ValueError when width < 1."""
    if width < 1:
        raise ValueError("width < 1")

    # Fast path (all work in C): valid when internal separators are single
    # spaces.  Stripping outer spaces makes the stripped text exactly the
    # words joined by single spaces.  A greedy regex match of up to width
    # chars ending at a word boundary is then exactly the maximal prefix
    # of words fitting in width, i.e. one output line.
    # Words longer than width, or any other mismatch, make the
    # reconstructed text differ from the stripped text, in which case we
    # fall through to the general loop below.
    if isinstance(width, int) and width <= 100000 and "  " not in text:
        stripped = text.strip(" ")
        if not stripped:
            return []
        lines = re.findall(
            r"(?s)[^ ].{0,%d}(?=(?: [^ ])|\Z)" % (width - 1), stripped
        )
        if " ".join(lines) == stripped:
            return lines

    # General path: track the current line length instead of joining a
    # candidate list for every word, and join each line only once.
    lines = []
    lines_append = lines.append
    cur = []
    cur_len = 0
    for w in text.split(" "):
        if not w:
            continue
        lw = len(w)
        if lw > width:
            if cur:
                lines_append(" ".join(cur))
                cur = []
                cur_len = 0
            start = 0
            while lw - start > width:
                lines_append(w[start:start + width])
                start += width
            if start:
                w = w[start:]
                lw -= start
        if cur:
            if cur_len + 1 + lw <= width:
                cur.append(w)
                cur_len += 1 + lw
            else:
                lines_append(" ".join(cur))
                cur = [w]
                cur_len = lw
        else:
            cur = [w]
            cur_len = lw
    if cur:
        lines_append(" ".join(cur))
    return lines
